note: agent-lifted from VB's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: WSS attenuation drift
concepts.gloss: A gradual change in a wavelength-selective switch's attenuation setting that reduces optical power on the channels passing through it.
concepts.example: A WSS intended to apply 3 dB attenuation drifts to 6 dB, causing its routed channel to leave the ROADM at low power.

concepts.label: WSS passband shift
concepts.gloss: Misalignment of a WSS or ROADM spectral passband with a channel, reducing that channel's quality despite normal measured power.
concepts.example: A 100 GHz WSS filter shifts away from a 193.1 THz carrier; the carrier power remains normal, but filtering penalties raise its errors.

concepts.label: WSS input port failure
concepts.gloss: Failure or blockage of a WSS input port that stops all channels arriving on the associated ROADM degree while leaving other degrees unaffected.
concepts.example: Input port 3 of a ROADM fails, blocking every channel from the east degree while west-degree traffic continues normally.

concepts.label: Transmit laser failure
synonyms: the far-end transmitter's laser has failed
concepts.gloss: Failure of the far-end transmitter laser that removes the optical signal for its transmitted channel.
concepts.example: The laser in a VB-TPD-400 at site A shuts down, so the far-end receiver at site B loses that channel.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: A complete hardware failure of a far-end card that loses its traffic and monitoring and may mask traffic alarms with an equipment alarm.
concepts.example: A remote VB-OTN-LC-400 card loses power, its transmitted channel and received traffic disappear, and no monitoring data is reported.

concepts.label: Receiver degradation
synonyms: degradation of this unit's own receiver
concepts.gloss: Deterioration of the local unit's optical receiver that introduces errors at that receiver without necessarily impairing the optical path or other receivers.
concepts.example: A degraded photodiode in one VB-MXP-400 reports pre-FEC errors although another receiver on the same optical path is normal.

concepts.label: a broken fibre
synonyms: the fibre section feeding this unit is broken
concepts.gloss: A physical break in the fibre section feeding a unit that prevents light from reaching its receiver.
concepts.example: A cable cut between two amplifier sites leaves the downstream line-amplifier input dark and raises loss-of-signal alarms.

concepts.label: a failed amplifier
synonyms: the preceding amplifier has failed and emits no light
concepts.gloss: Failure of the preceding optical amplifier such that it emits no light into the downstream channel path.
concepts.example: An inline amplifier loses its pump and its output goes dark, so the next preamplifier receives no light.

concepts.label: a disconnected patch cord
synonyms: the patch cord may have been disconnected
concepts.gloss: An unplugged optical patch cord at a multiplex-section input that opens the channel path and prevents light reaching the receiver.
concepts.example: A technician removes the patch cord feeding the preamplifier, causing OMS_LOS_P because no light reaches its input.

concepts.label: a rise in fibre loss
concepts.gloss: A sharp increase in attenuation on the fibre feeding a unit that weakens and impairs the received optical signal.
concepts.example: A severe fibre bend adds 7 dB loss, lowering received power and OSNR until OTU_SD is raised.

concepts.label: a rise in an amplifier's noise
concepts.gloss: An increase in noise contributed by an amplifier on the channel path that degrades optical signal quality.
concepts.example: An ageing inline amplifier develops a higher noise figure, reducing downstream OSNR and producing pre-FEC errors.

concepts.label: a rise in differential group delay
concepts.gloss: An increase in differential group delay along the channel path that creates polarization-mode-dispersion impairment.
concepts.example: Changing fibre conditions raise DGD from 5 ps to 35 ps, causing the receiver to lose OTU frame alignment.

concepts.label: a fast polarisation transient
concepts.gloss: A rapid polarization transient on the channel path whose rate exceeds the receiver's tracking capability.
concepts.example: A fibre disturbance rotates polarization faster than the coherent receiver can track, producing errored seconds.

concepts.label: a dirty connector
concepts.gloss: Contamination on an optical connector in the channel path that adds loss or reflection and impairs the signal.
concepts.example: Dust on an LC connector lowers OSNR enough for pre-FEC errors to cross the OTU_SD threshold.

concepts.label: any failure
concepts.gloss: An intentionally broad probable-cause category covering any underlying failure that can trigger the associated status or alarm.
concepts.example: PROT_ACTIVE is attributed to any failure on the working path when the exact failed component has not yet been identified.

concepts.label: failure
concepts.gloss: A generic equipment hardware failure used when an alarm identifies the failed component class but not a more specific mechanism.
concepts.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL reports a card failure even though diagnostics cannot distinguish a processor fault from a power-rail fault.

concepts.label: Pump or unit failure
concepts.gloss: A complete optical-amplifier failure caused either by its pump subsystem or by the amplifier unit, resulting in lost output and carried traffic.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-ILA suffers an internal or pump failure, its output goes dark, and all channels it carried are lost.

concepts.label: failure of this unit's pump laser
concepts.gloss: Failure of the pump laser within the local optical amplifier that prevents amplification despite light being present at the input.
concepts.example: A preamplifier still receives the multiplexed signal, but its failed pump produces no optical output and raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: failure of the unit itself
concepts.gloss: Failure of the local amplifier unit apart from the specifically identified pump-laser mechanism, leaving input light present but no output.
concepts.example: An internal amplifier power-supply fault makes a VB-OA-BST output dark even though its input remains illuminated.

concepts.label: Gain loss
concepts.gloss: Loss of gain in the local amplifier that lowers output power and consequently reduces the signal-to-noise ratio of its channels.
concepts.example: An inline amplifier configured for 20 dB gain delivers only 17 dB, producing AMP_GAIN_OOR and weaker downstream channels.

concepts.label: Pump ageing
concepts.gloss: Progressive deterioration of an amplifier pump that requires increasing drive current to maintain the configured gain.
concepts.example: A booster raises pump current from 100% to 121% of its beginning-of-life value and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: Gain tilt
concepts.gloss: A non-flat amplifier gain profile that makes some wavelengths, especially channels at a band edge, weaker than others.
concepts.example: A booster gives C-band edge channels 3 dB less gain than central channels, affecting only that subset.

concepts.label: Switch fabric failure
concepts.gloss: Failure of an OTN switch's ODU cross-connect fabric that interrupts ODUs traversing it and causes AIS to be forwarded.
concepts.example: The VB-OTNSW fabric fails, interrupting every cross-connected ODU and sending AIS toward their client ports.

concepts.label: Wrong cross-connection
concepts.gloss: An erroneous ODU cross-connect configuration that sends one ODU to an unintended destination without an optical-layer symptom.
concepts.example: ODU2 from client A is mapped to client C instead of client B, causing a trail-trace mismatch while optical power remains normal.

concepts.label: Client port failure
synonyms: a failure of the client port
concepts.gloss: Failure of a client-facing port or its optic that takes down the associated client service.
concepts.example: The 100GE optic on VB-CP-100GE fails, producing EQPT_PORT_FAIL and loss of the mapped client service.

concepts.label: An impairment affecting the whole incoming line
concepts.gloss: An optical impairment present across the entire incoming multiplexed line rather than on only one wavelength.
concepts.example: Excess loss before a ROADM degrades the whole incoming WDM line, so every channel routed onward retains an impairment.

concepts.label: continues, after the node, as an impairment of each channel routed onwards
concepts.gloss: Persistence after a node of an incoming line impairment on each individual channel that the node routes onward.
concepts.example: A low-OSNR incoming line enters a ROADM, and all demultiplexed channels leaving on different degrees remain low-OSNR.

concepts.label: A power loss upstream of up to about 8 dB
concepts.gloss: An upstream optical-power reduction of roughly 8 dB or less that a node can re-level, although the associated OSNR penalty remains.
concepts.example: A 6 dB upstream loss is compensated at the node so downstream power is nominal, but the lost OSNR is not recovered.

concepts.label: is re-levelled at the node
concepts.gloss: A condition in which a node adjusts an incoming signal back to its target optical power.
concepts.example: After receiving a channel 5 dB low, the node increases gain so it leaves at the configured 0 dBm level.

concepts.label: does not appear downstream as low power
concepts.gloss: A downstream state in which prior power loss is no longer visible as low optical power because the signal has been re-levelled.
concepts.example: The amplifier restores a weak input channel to nominal output power, so downstream monitoring does not report low power.

concepts.label: the loss of signal-to-noise ratio it caused remains
concepts.gloss: The residual signal-to-noise-ratio degradation that remains after optical power has been restored.
concepts.example: A channel is amplified back to 0 dBm, but its OSNR remains 4 dB below baseline because amplification cannot remove accumulated noise.

concepts.label: A larger loss
concepts.gloss: An upstream attenuation greater than the node's compensable range that results in downstream low power.
concepts.example: A 12 dB fibre loss exceeds the node's 8 dB re-levelling range, so the outgoing channel remains weak.

concepts.label: power is low
concepts.gloss: An optical state in which one channel or all channels have power below their expected operating level.
concepts.example: Channel 37 is measured at -18 dBm instead of -10 dBm after WSS attenuation drift.

concepts.label: pass through the node unchanged
concepts.gloss: A state in which signals traverse the node without the relevant property or impairment being altered.
concepts.example: Channels not selected by a ROADM operation retain the same power and quality after passing through the node.

concepts.label: power is normal
concepts.gloss: A per-channel state in which measured optical power remains within its expected range despite another possible impairment.
concepts.example: A passband-shifted channel still measures -5 dBm, which is nominal, even though its pre-FEC BER has risen.

concepts.label: signal quality is reduced
concepts.gloss: A per-channel degradation of usable optical signal quality, such as filtering penalty or reduced margin, independent of absolute power.
concepts.example: A channel has normal power but reduced Q-factor after traversing a misaligned WSS passband.

concepts.label: is blocked
concepts.gloss: A state in which every channel arriving on a particular ROADM degree is prevented from passing at that location.
concepts.example: A failed WSS input blocks all eight wavelengths entering on the east degree.

concepts.label: are unaffected
concepts.gloss: A state indicating that channels on ROADM degrees other than the failed or impaired degree continue without impact.
concepts.example: When the east input port fails, channels arriving from the north and west degrees remain in service.

concepts.label: no light reaches the receiver
synonyms: No light at the line receiver.
no light arrives at its input
no light arrives at the input of the receiving end of the multiplex section
concepts.gloss: Absence of optical energy at a receiver input, causing loss-of-signal declaration and loss of frame alignment.
concepts.example: After a fibre cut, the line receiver reads no input power, declares G.798 dLOS, and loses OTU framing.

concepts.label: declares loss of signal (G.798 dLOS)
concepts.gloss: The G.798 loss-of-signal defect declared by an optical receiver when received light is absent or below the detection criterion.
concepts.example: A dark receiver input causes the transponder to assert dLOS and raise OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: frame alignment is lost
synonyms: OTU frame alignment lost while light is present.
concepts.gloss: Loss of OTU frame synchronization at a receiver, whether from absent light or a severely impaired signal, which triggers downstream AIS and backward defect indication.
concepts.example: High pre-FEC errors prevent OTU header recognition, so the unit inserts ODU-AIS downstream and sends BDI upstream.

concepts.label: the unit itself has failed
concepts.gloss: A state in which the local equipment unit has failed, producing an equipment defect and masking resulting traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A line card processor fails, declares dEQ, loses frame alignment, and suppresses secondary traffic alarms.

concepts.label: declares an equipment defect (dEQ)
concepts.gloss: The dEQ defect declared when the equipment detects an internal unit-level hardware failure.
concepts.example: A card self-test detects a failed FPGA and asserts dEQ.

concepts.label: the unit's traffic alarms are masked by the equipment alarm
synonyms: are masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: Suppression of a unit's secondary traffic alarms because a higher-level equipment alarm already identifies the primary failure.
concepts.example: After EQPT_CARD_FAIL is raised, derivative OTU traffic alarms from the dead card are masked.

concepts.label: the signal arrives but is impaired
synonyms: lower power, a lower signal-to-noise ratio, a raised differential group delay, a filtering penalty from a misaligned or narrowed passband, a receiver-side penalty, or a slow loss of margin
concepts.gloss: A state in which an optical signal is still received but suffers enough power, OSNR, DGD, filtering, receiver, or margin degradation to cause errors or framing loss.
concepts.example: A noisy amplifier leaves light present, but low OSNR produces pre-FEC errors and eventually OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: pre-FEC errors appear
synonyms: Signal degraded: pre-FEC errors above threshold
concepts.gloss: A received-signal degradation state in which bit errors measured before forward-error correction exceed the configured threshold.
concepts.example: The pre-FEC BER rises to 2×10^-3 for a channel and triggers OTU_SD.

concepts.label: Polarisation changes faster than the tracking range
concepts.gloss: A state in which signal polarization changes more rapidly than the receiver's polarization tracker can follow.
concepts.example: Mechanical vibration causes rapid state-of-polarization rotation and a burst of errored seconds.

concepts.label: produce errored seconds
concepts.gloss: Performance intervals containing one or more received bit or block errors due to signal impairment.
concepts.example: A polarization transient causes errors during 12 separate seconds in a 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: an ODU alarm indication signal is inserted downstream
concepts.gloss: Insertion of an ODU alarm indication signal into downstream ODU traffic as a consequent action for an upstream OTU defect.
concepts.example: On OTU frame loss, the line card sends ODU-AIS on each ODU carried by that OTU.

concepts.label: a backward defect indication is sent
concepts.gloss: Transmission of a backward defect indication toward the remote transmitter to report a defect detected at the receiving end.
concepts.example: Site B loses OTU framing and sends BDI back to site A, where OTU_BDI is reported.

concepts.label: loses the signal
concepts.gloss: Complete loss, at the far-end receiver, of the particular optical channel sent by a failed transmitter.
concepts.example: Failure of the site-A laser causes site B to lose only that 400G channel.

concepts.label: is lost
concepts.gloss: Complete unavailability of the relevant transmitted channel, received traffic, carried channels, or client service.
concepts.example: A failed line card loses its transmitted wavelength and all client traffic mapped through it.

concepts.label: goes silent
concepts.gloss: Absence of telemetry or status reports from monitoring associated with a failed unit.
concepts.example: After a remote card loses power, its performance counters stop updating and monitoring goes silent.

concepts.label: Errors appear
concepts.gloss: Errors observed only at the local receiver, indicating receiver-local degradation rather than a shared optical-path problem.
concepts.example: One receiver reports increasing pre-FEC errors while another receiver connected to the same path remains normal.

concepts.label: are normal
concepts.gloss: An unaffected state in which the referenced other channels or optical path remain within normal operating limits.
concepts.example: Only one receiver is degraded; the optical path and all other channels retain normal power and error rates.

concepts.label: The far end reports a defect on the signal this unit transmits.
concepts.gloss: A received backward indication that the far end has detected a defect on the signal transmitted by the local unit.
concepts.example: The local transponder raises OTU_BDI after its remote peer reports inability to receive the local OTU correctly.

concepts.label: The unit has detected a fault in its transmit laser.
concepts.gloss: A local equipment state indicating that diagnostics have detected a fault in the unit's transmit laser.
concepts.example: Laser-bias monitoring detects no optical output and causes EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: Card hardware fault.
concepts.gloss: A detected internal hardware fault affecting an equipment card as a whole.
concepts.example: A failed card power rail is detected and raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: All three units operate
concepts.gloss: The operating state in which all three amplifier stages or units in the relevant arrangement are functioning and maintain constant gain.
concepts.example: The booster, inline amplifier, and preamplifier are all operational and each runs in constant-gain mode.

concepts.label: constant-gain mode
concepts.gloss: An amplifier control mode that adjusts pump drive to maintain a configured optical gain despite input or component changes.
concepts.example: When input power falls by 2 dB, the amplifier increases pump drive to preserve its 20 dB gain.

concepts.label: less light arrives at the input
concepts.gloss: A reduction in total optical power arriving at an amplifier input, leading to weaker and noisier output under the relevant operating conditions.
concepts.example: A fibre loss reduces amplifier input by 5 dB, so less light leaves and the output OSNR worsens.

concepts.label: the optical signal-to-noise ratio of every channel falls as well
concepts.gloss: A reduction in optical signal-to-noise ratio across every channel carried by the affected amplifier or unit.
concepts.example: Loss of amplifier gain reduces OSNR by 2 dB on all 80 WDM channels.

concepts.label: Loss of the OSC on one section
synonyms: the supervisory channel is not received
concepts.gloss: Failure to receive the optical supervisory channel on one fibre section, localizing a supervisory-connectivity problem to that section.
concepts.example: An inline amplifier detects no OSC from the upstream span and raises OSC_LOS.

concepts.label: does not propagate to the next
concepts.gloss: A property of a section-local condition whereby it is terminated or regenerated and is not passed to the following section.
concepts.example: OSC loss is reported on span A–B, but node B originates a new OSC toward C, so the loss does not propagate.

concepts.label: no light leaves
concepts.gloss: A dark optical output from a unit, indicating that no light leaves its output port.
concepts.example: A failed booster measures normal input light but zero output power.

concepts.label: the output is noisier
concepts.gloss: An output state with increased optical noise relative to the signal, commonly following weak amplifier input.
concepts.example: After input power drops, amplified spontaneous emission dominates more strongly and output OSNR declines.

concepts.label: raises its drive current to hold the gain
concepts.gloss: An amplifier response in which pump-laser drive current is increased to preserve gain as the pump ages or conditions change.
concepts.example: The amplifier raises pump current from 100% to 112% of beginning-of-life current while holding 20 dB gain.

concepts.label: Traffic is unaffected until the drive current reaches its limit
concepts.gloss: A state in which carried traffic remains serviceable while increased pump current still has enough headroom to maintain gain.
concepts.example: At 115% pump current the amplifier meets its gain target, so all channels continue without errors.

concepts.label: gives early warning
concepts.gloss: A trend-based indication that exposes developing equipment deterioration before it disrupts traffic.
concepts.example: A month-long rise in pump current warns operators of pump ageing before any channel is lost.

concepts.label: leads eventually to the end-of-life alarm (AMP_PUMP_EOL)
concepts.gloss: The eventual AMP_PUMP_EOL indication produced when an ageing pump reaches its defined end-of-life current threshold.
concepts.example: Continued current growth crosses 120% of beginning-of-life value and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: arrive weaker than the others
concepts.gloss: A gain-tilt condition in which channels at one edge of the optical band arrive at lower power than other channels.
concepts.example: Channels near 191.4 THz arrive 3 dB weaker than channels near the band center.

concepts.label: are affected
concepts.gloss: A partial-impact state applying to some channels in a set rather than to every channel.
concepts.example: Gain tilt degrades the five lowest-frequency channels while the remaining 75 stay normal.

concepts.label: light is present at its input but none leaves its output
concepts.gloss: An amplifier failure signature in which optical light is present at the input but no light emerges from the output.
concepts.example: The preamplifier input reads -20 dBm while its output reads dark, causing AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: the gain departs from its set point by more than 2 dB
concepts.gloss: An amplifier out-of-range state in which actual gain differs from its configured set point by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: A 20 dB set point with measured gain of 17.5 dB triggers AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: the pump drive current exceeds 120 per cent of its beginning-of-life value
concepts.gloss: An amplifier end-of-life threshold state in which pump drive current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: A pump originally requiring 500 mA now requires 610 mA, or 122%, and satisfies the alarm criterion.

concepts.label: an ODU alarm indication signal
synonyms: An ODU alarm indication signal is received.
concepts.gloss: Receipt of an ODU alarm indication signal that substitutes a standardized failure pattern for unavailable upstream ODU traffic.
concepts.example: A client port receives ODU-AIS after an upstream OTU loses frame alignment.

concepts.label: carries an ODU alarm indication signal onwards on every ODU cross-connected through it
synonyms: an alarm indication signal is carried onwards
concepts.gloss: Forwarding of ODU-AIS on every affected ODU as those ODUs traverse an OTN cross-connect.
concepts.example: The switch receives AIS on four cross-connected ODUs and carries AIS onward on each corresponding egress.

concepts.label: an ODU delivered from the wrong source
concepts.gloss: A state in which an ODU arriving at a destination originates from a source other than the one provisioned or expected.
concepts.example: Client B expects ODU from client A but receives the trail trace of client C.

concepts.label: The client service has failed.
concepts.gloss: Loss of the end-client service due to a client-port, ODU-path, cross-connect, or upstream failure.
concepts.example: A 100GE customer circuit goes down when its mapped ODU receives AIS.

concepts.label: the service is protected
concepts.gloss: A service configuration with a redundant path that permits recovery from a defect by switching paths.
concepts.example: A protected ODU uses its standby path after the working fibre fails.

concepts.label: the selector can choose a path free of defects
concepts.gloss: Availability of at least one selectable service path that has no detected defects.
concepts.example: The working path has AIS, but the protection path is healthy, so the selector can choose it.

concepts.label: the service suffers only a brief hit while the selector switches
concepts.gloss: A short service interruption limited to the selector's protection-switching interval.
concepts.example: Traffic drops for 35 ms while the ODU selector changes from the working to the protection path.

concepts.label: is interrupted
concepts.gloss: Loss of traffic on every ODU cross-connected through a failed switch fabric.
concepts.example: A VB-OTNSW fabric outage interrupts all ODUs traversing that switch.

concepts.label: an alarm indication signal is carried onwards
concepts.gloss: A state in which an alarm indication signal is forwarded on each affected connection instead of valid payload.
concepts.example: Following a fabric failure, each downstream ODU carries AIS toward its client.

concepts.label: is delivered to the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: Delivery of one ODU to an unintended endpoint because of an incorrect cross-connection.
concepts.example: An ODU intended for port 2 appears at port 7.

concepts.label: There is no optical symptom.
concepts.gloss: Absence of abnormal optical power or quality indications despite a logical ODU routing error.
concepts.example: A misrouted ODU has normal optical power and OSNR, so only the trail-trace mismatch reveals the fault.

concepts.label: fails
concepts.gloss: A hardware-failure state of a client optic or its containing client port.
concepts.example: The 400GE pluggable stops transmitting and the associated client port enters a failed state.

concepts.label: The far end reports that it is receiving an alarm indication signal.
concepts.gloss: An ODU-layer backward defect report indicating that the far end is receiving ODU-AIS.
concepts.example: The remote endpoint receives AIS and returns ODU-BDI to the local client port.

concepts.label: Trail trace identifier mismatch: the ODU received is not the one expected.
concepts.gloss: An ODU trail-trace mismatch showing that the received ODU identity differs from the provisioned expectation.
concepts.example: The expected trace is CUSTOMER_A but the received trace is CUSTOMER_B, raising ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: The selector is on the protection path.
concepts.gloss: A protection status in which the service selector currently uses the protection ODU path rather than the working path.
concepts.example: After a working-path failure, the selector switches to the standby ODU and reports PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: The protection path has failed.
concepts.gloss: A protection status indicating that the protection ODU path itself has failed and cannot provide redundancy.
concepts.example: Loss of signal on the standby route causes PROT_UNAVAIL while traffic still uses the working route.

concepts.label: Port hardware fault.
concepts.gloss: A hardware defect detected within a client port or its associated port electronics.
concepts.example: A failed serializer on a 100GE client port raises EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: Fabric fault.
concepts.gloss: A hardware defect detected in the OTN switch's internal cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: An internal fabric ASIC fails self-test and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.

concepts.label: the power of every channel
concepts.gloss: Per-wavelength optical power measured for every monitored channel at a channel-monitoring-capable node.
concepts.example: A ROADM reports channel 21 at -4.8 dBm and channel 22 at -5.1 dBm.

concepts.label: the OSNR of every channel
concepts.gloss: Estimated optical signal-to-noise ratio for each channel, available with channel or advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: Advanced monitoring estimates the 193.1 THz channel's OSNR as 18.7 dB.

concepts.label: Received power
concepts.gloss: The optical power measured at a unit's receiver input when power monitoring is available.
concepts.example: A transponder reports received optical power of -14.2 dBm.

concepts.label: errored seconds, in 15-minute bins
concepts.gloss: The count of seconds containing errors, accumulated in 15-minute performance-monitoring bins on all units.
concepts.example: The 10:00–10:15 bin records 12 errored seconds.

concepts.label: pre-FEC bit error ratio
concepts.gloss: The bit error ratio measured before forward-error correction by a unit with advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: A coherent receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 1.6×10^-3.

concepts.label: differential group delay
concepts.gloss: The measured differential group delay of a received optical channel, available through advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: The receiver reports DGD of 28 ps during a polarization-mode-dispersion event.

concepts.label: polarisation change rate
concepts.gloss: The measured rate of change of the received signal's state of polarization, available through advanced monitoring.
concepts.example: Monitoring records a polarization rotation rate above the receiver's tracking threshold during a fibre disturbance.

concepts.label: Total optical power at the unit's input
concepts.gloss: Total aggregate optical power across all wavelengths at an amplifier or unit input.
concepts.example: A line amplifier reports total input power of -8 dBm for the incoming WDM band.

concepts.label: Total optical power at the unit's output
concepts.gloss: Total aggregate optical power across all wavelengths at an amplifier or unit output.
concepts.example: A booster reports total output power of +20 dBm.

concepts.label: Drive current of the pump laser, as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value
concepts.gloss: Pump-laser drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value and used as an amplifier-health indicator.
concepts.example: An ageing preamplifier reports pump current at 118% of its original value.

concepts.label: Presence of the supervisory channel at the input
concepts.gloss: A Boolean or status measurement indicating whether the optical supervisory channel is present at a unit input.
concepts.example: An inline amplifier reports OSC presence=false after an upstream fibre break.

concepts.label: client errored seconds
concepts.gloss: The number of client-side errored seconds reported per 15-minute interval by a client port.
concepts.example: A 100GE port reports 4 client errored seconds for the latest 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: client unavailable seconds
concepts.gloss: The number of client-side unavailable seconds reported per 15-minute interval by a client port.
concepts.example: A failed client port records 900 unavailable seconds in a complete 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: ROADM
concepts.gloss: A colourless, directionless and contentionless reconfigurable optical add/drop node that independently switches wavelength channels and can monitor channel power and OSNR.
concepts.example: VB-ROADM-CDC routes a 193.1 THz channel from the east degree to the west degree while measuring its power.

concepts.label: Transponder
concepts.gloss: An optical terminal unit that maps client traffic onto a line-side wavelength and contains transmit-laser, card, and receiver functions.
concepts.example: VB-TPD-400 converts a 400G client signal into a coherent line channel.

concepts.label: Muxponder
concepts.gloss: An optical terminal that multiplexes multiple lower-rate client signals into a higher-rate line channel and can experience laser, card, or receiver faults.
concepts.example: VB-MXP-400 combines four 100GE clients into one 400G optical line signal.

concepts.label: OTN line card
concepts.gloss: A card providing OTN line transmission and reception, including an optical transmitter, receiver, and card-level hardware.
concepts.example: VB-OTN-LC-400 terminates a 400G OTU and carries several ODUs.

concepts.label: All units
concepts.gloss: The collective class of optical units that provide common received-power, error, pre-FEC BER, DGD, and polarization-rate monitoring capabilities as applicable.
concepts.example: A VB transponder is treated as one of all units that can report received power and errored seconds.

concepts.label: Booster amplifier (BA)
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier placed after the transmitting ROADM to launch a multiplex section at the required power.
concepts.example: VB-OA-BST amplifies the outgoing WDM band before it enters the long-haul fibre.

concepts.label: At the transmitting end of a multiplex section, after the ROADM
concepts.gloss: The network position at the transmit end of a multiplex section between the ROADM output and outgoing fibre.
concepts.example: The VB-OA-BST installed immediately after the site-A ROADM occupies the booster position.

concepts.label: Line amplifier (LA)
concepts.gloss: An inline optical amplifier at an intermediate site that restores WDM signal power along a multiplex section.
concepts.example: VB-OA-ILA at the midpoint of an 80 km span boosts all carried wavelengths.

concepts.label: At intermediate amplifier sites
concepts.gloss: An intermediate location along an optical route where an inline amplifier is installed rather than at either terminal ROADM.
concepts.example: A hut halfway between sites A and B is the line-amplifier position.

concepts.label: Preamplifier (PA)
concepts.gloss: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of a multiplex section, before the ROADM, that boosts the incoming WDM signal.
concepts.example: VB-OA-PRE amplifies the incoming band before it enters the destination ROADM.

concepts.label: At the receiving end of a multiplex section, before the ROADM
concepts.gloss: The network position at the receive end of a multiplex section between the incoming fibre and the ROADM.
concepts.example: The amplifier directly before site-B's ROADM occupies the preamplifier position.

concepts.label: OTN switch
concepts.gloss: An ODU-layer cross-connect fabric that switches ODU trails independently of the optical wavelengths carrying them.
concepts.example: VB-OTNSW cross-connects an incoming ODU2 from line card 1 to client port 8.

concepts.label: Client port, 10GE
concepts.gloss: A client-facing Ethernet port operating at 10 Gigabit Ethernet and subject to client-port hardware failure.
concepts.example: VB-CP-10GE accepts a customer's 10GE signal for mapping into an ODU.

concepts.label: Client port, 100GE
concepts.gloss: A client-facing Ethernet port operating at 100 Gigabit Ethernet and subject to client-port hardware failure.
concepts.example: VB-CP-100GE terminates a 100GE customer circuit on a muxponder.

concepts.label: Client port, 400GE
concepts.gloss: A client-facing Ethernet port operating at 400 Gigabit Ethernet and subject to client-port hardware failure.
concepts.example: VB-CP-400GE receives a 400GE client signal for OTN transport.

concepts.label: client port
concepts.gloss: The generic client-facing service interface that can fail and reports client errored and unavailable seconds.
concepts.example: A client port carrying a 100GE service reports 3 errored seconds and 0 unavailable seconds in a 15-minute bin.

concepts.label: OCH_LOS
concepts.gloss: A critical optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm raised when an optical unit receives no light, with likely causes along the transmitter-to-receiver path.
concepts.example: A fibre cut makes a VB-TPD-400 receiver dark and raises OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: OTU_LOF
concepts.gloss: A critical OTU loss-of-frame alarm raised when a unit cannot maintain OTU frame alignment because of severe path or receiver impairment.
concepts.example: High DGD prevents frame synchronization and raises OTU_LOF on the receiving line card.

concepts.label: OTU_SD
concepts.gloss: A minor OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when pre-FEC errors exceed threshold while the OTU remains frame-aligned.
concepts.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER above the configured limit and triggers OTU_SD.

concepts.label: OTU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A non-alarmed OTU status indication that the far end has reported a defect on the locally transmitted OTU signal.
concepts.example: Site B loses the OTU from site A and sends BDI, causing site A to report OTU_BDI without alarm severity.

concepts.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical equipment alarm indicating that the local unit has detected failure of its transmit laser.
concepts.example: Laser output drops to zero on a transponder and EQPT_TX_FAIL is raised.

concepts.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical equipment alarm indicating a generic hardware failure of a card.
concepts.example: A line-card FPGA fails self-test and the unit raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
concepts.gloss: A critical line-amplifier alarm indicating that no optical light is present at its input, usually because of upstream fibre loss or amplifier failure.
concepts.example: A cable cut ahead of a VB-OA-ILA causes AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: OMS_LOS_P
concepts.gloss: A critical preamplifier alarm indicating loss of the incoming optical multiplex-section signal.
concepts.example: A disconnected receive-side patch cord leaves the VB-OA-PRE input dark and raises OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: OSC_LOS
concepts.gloss: A major line-amplifier or preamplifier alarm indicating absence of the optical supervisory channel on the feeding fibre section.
concepts.example: The payload remains marginally present, but the preamplifier cannot detect the OSC and raises OSC_LOS.

concepts.label: AMP_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical amplifier alarm raised when input light is present but the booster, line amplifier, or preamplifier produces no output due to pump or unit failure.
concepts.example: A VB-OA-BST has illuminated input and dark output after pump failure, raising AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
concepts.gloss: A minor line-amplifier or preamplifier alarm raised when measured gain differs from its set point by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: A preamplifier set to 20 dB produces 17 dB gain and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
concepts.gloss: A minor amplifier end-of-life alarm raised when pump drive current exceeds 120% of its beginning-of-life value because of ageing.
concepts.example: A booster reaches 122% pump current and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL before traffic fails.

concepts.label: CLIENT_SF
concepts.gloss: A critical client service-failure alarm raised by a client port when its service is down due to port, path, cross-connect, fabric, or other failure.
concepts.example: A switch-fabric failure removes a 100GE service and its client port raises CLIENT_SF.

concepts.label: ODU_AIS
concepts.gloss: A non-alarmed client-port indication that an ODU alarm indication signal has been received.
concepts.example: An upstream OTU failure sends AIS to the client port, which reports ODU_AIS.

concepts.label: ODU_BDI
concepts.gloss: A non-alarmed client-port indication that the far end reports receiving ODU-AIS.
concepts.example: The remote ODU endpoint receives AIS and returns BDI, causing the local port to report ODU_BDI.

concepts.label: ODU_TIM
concepts.gloss: A major client-port alarm indicating that the received ODU trail trace does not match the expected ODU identity, commonly because of a wrong cross-connection.
concepts.example: A port expecting CUSTOMER_A receives CUSTOMER_B's trace and raises ODU_TIM.

concepts.label: PROT_ACTIVE
concepts.gloss: A minor client-port status alarm indicating that service traffic is currently selected from the protection path.
concepts.example: After working-path loss, the selector switches to standby and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
concepts.gloss: A minor client-port alarm indicating that the protection path has failed and is unavailable for recovery.
concepts.example: A fibre cut on the standby ODU route raises PROT_UNAVAIL.

concepts.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical client-port equipment alarm indicating a generic hardware fault in that port.
concepts.example: A failed 100GE port ASIC causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
concepts.gloss: A critical OTN-switch equipment alarm indicating a hardware fault in the ODU cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric ASIC failure on VB-OTNSW raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL and interrupts cross-connected ODUs.

concepts.label: that channel
concepts.gloss: The single optical wavelength channel directly associated with the condition being described.
concepts.example: A WSS passband shift reduces quality only on the affected 193.1 THz channel.

concepts.label: Every channel arriving at the node on that degree
concepts.gloss: All wavelength channels entering a ROADM node through the particular degree or directional input under discussion.
concepts.example: A failed east-degree WSS port blocks every channel arriving from the east.

concepts.label: channels arriving on the other degrees
concepts.gloss: Channels entering the same ROADM through directional degrees other than the affected degree.
concepts.example: After the east input fails, traffic arriving on the north and west degrees remains unaffected.

concepts.label: The channel it transmits
concepts.gloss: The specific line-side optical channel generated and sent by the referenced unit.
concepts.example: A transponder laser failure loses the 400G channel that the transponder transmits.

concepts.label: the traffic it receives
concepts.gloss: The payload traffic arriving at and being terminated or processed by the referenced unit.
concepts.example: A card failure discards all client traffic the card was receiving.

concepts.label: its monitoring
concepts.gloss: The telemetry, status, and performance reporting functions belonging to the referenced unit.
concepts.example: When a card loses power, its monitoring stops sending counters to the management system.

concepts.label: its traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: Alarms derived from traffic or signal defects on the referenced unit, as distinct from equipment alarms.
concepts.example: OTU_LOF is masked after a higher-level card equipment defect is declared.

concepts.label: this receiver only
concepts.gloss: Impact confined to the particular local receiver rather than the shared optical path or other receivers.
concepts.example: A degraded photodiode causes errors on receiver A only.

concepts.label: other channels
concepts.gloss: Channels in the same system other than the specifically affected channel.
concepts.example: A single-channel passband fault leaves the other 79 wavelengths normal.

concepts.label: the optical path
concepts.gloss: The end-to-end optical transmission route, including fibre, amplifiers, connectors, and switching elements.
concepts.example: Receiver-local errors occur even though measurements show the optical path is normal.

concepts.label: the unit
concepts.gloss: The single equipment unit whose state or control action is being described.
concepts.example: Pump ageing causes the affected amplifier unit to raise its drive current.

concepts.label: Every channel carried by the unit
concepts.gloss: All optical channels transported through the referenced amplifier or transmission unit.
concepts.example: A complete amplifier failure loses every one of its 80 carried channels.

concepts.label: every channel
concepts.gloss: The complete set of wavelength channels in the relevant line or unit, with no exceptions.
concepts.example: Loss of amplifier gain lowers OSNR on every channel in the WDM band.

concepts.label: Traffic
concepts.gloss: The user payload being transported, independently of monitoring or equipment-health indications.
concepts.example: Rising pump current leaves traffic unaffected while gain is still maintained.

concepts.label: the trend
concepts.gloss: The time-series progression of a monitored value used to identify developing or eventual failure.
concepts.example: The upward pump-current trend provides warning months before the end-of-life threshold.

concepts.label: channels at one edge of the band
concepts.gloss: The subset of wavelength channels located near one frequency edge of the amplified optical band.
concepts.example: Gain tilt makes the five lowest-frequency band-edge channels weaker.

concepts.label: Some channels, not all
concepts.gloss: A proper subset of channels, explicitly fewer than all channels in the relevant set.
concepts.example: Only 6 of 80 channels are impaired by gain tilt.

concepts.label: Every ODU cross-connected through the switch
concepts.gloss: All ODU containers whose routes pass through the referenced OTN switch fabric.
concepts.example: A fabric outage interrupts every ODU cross-connected through VB-OTNSW.

concepts.label: each
concepts.gloss: Each individual member of the contextually defined affected set, considered one by one.
concepts.example: The switch forwards AIS on each of the four ODUs traversing the failed connection set.

concepts.label: one ODU
concepts.gloss: A single ODU trail or container rather than all ODUs carried by the system.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connection misroutes one ODU while the remaining ODUs are correct.

concepts.label: The client optic
concepts.gloss: The optical transceiver or pluggable module implementing the client-facing physical interface.
concepts.example: A failed 100GE QSFP is the affected client optic.

concepts.label: the port
concepts.gloss: The specific physical or logical client interface associated with the condition.
concepts.example: A serializer fault causes only port 4 to fail.

concepts.label: the client service
concepts.gloss: The customer-facing service carried through a client port and its associated ODU path.
concepts.example: A 100GE customer circuit is the client service lost after ODU-AIS.

concepts.label: after the node
concepts.gloss: The downstream side of a network node after its switching, amplification, or re-levelling functions have been applied.
concepts.example: Channel power is checked after the ROADM to determine whether upstream loss was re-levelled.

concepts.label: there
concepts.gloss: The same local point previously identified in the diagnostic context, rather than a distinct named network location.
concepts.example: Channels are blocked at the failed WSS input, and the blockage is observed there.

concepts.label: The receiver at the far end
concepts.gloss: The remote receiver that terminates the optical channel sent from the local transmitter.
concepts.example: The far-end receiver at site B loses the channel when site A's laser fails.

concepts.label: the far end
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint of the monitored connection relative to the current unit or management observation point.
concepts.example: A card failure at site B is described from site A as occurring at the far end.

concepts.label: here
concepts.gloss: The local observation point or node from which the diagnostic statement is made.
concepts.example: BDI is received here at site A after site B detects a defect.

concepts.label: this receiver
concepts.gloss: The specific local receiver currently being diagnosed or reporting the condition.
concepts.example: Errors appear at this receiver while a parallel receiver remains normal.

concepts.label: the far-end transmitter
concepts.gloss: The remote transmitter whose optical signal is expected at the local receiver.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS may result because the far-end transmitter's laser has failed.

concepts.label: along the channel's path
concepts.gloss: Any point along the end-to-end optical route followed by a particular wavelength channel.
concepts.example: A dirty connector midway along the channel path lowers that channel's OSNR.

concepts.label: the line receiver
concepts.gloss: The line-side optical receiver that terminates an incoming wavelength or OTU signal.
concepts.example: No light at the line receiver causes dLOS.

concepts.label: this unit's own receiver
concepts.gloss: The receiver integrated into the unit currently under diagnosis, as opposed to a remote receiver or the path.
concepts.example: A degraded photodiode in the unit's own receiver causes local-only errors.

concepts.label: on the path to the far end
concepts.gloss: A position somewhere on the transmission path between the local unit and its remote endpoint.
concepts.example: A fibre defect on the path to the far end causes the remote receiver to lose signal.

concepts.label: the signal this unit transmits
concepts.gloss: The outbound signal generated by the local unit and observed or diagnosed as an object of the far-end report.
concepts.example: The far end reports a defect on the signal this unit transmits.

concepts.label: this unit
concepts.gloss: The local equipment instance currently reporting or undergoing the fault, rather than another unit on the path.
concepts.example: AMP_FAIL diagnostics show that the pump failure is in this preamplifier.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: The particular local equipment card associated with the current alarm or diagnostic context.
concepts.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL identifies a hardware fault on this line card.

concepts.label: the output
concepts.gloss: The optical egress interface of a unit where emitted light or output power is observed.
concepts.example: No light is measured at the failed amplifier's output.

concepts.label: downstream
concepts.gloss: The direction or network region following the current unit in the direction of traffic flow.
concepts.example: On frame loss, ODU-AIS is inserted downstream toward the client.

concepts.label: the fibre section feeding this unit
concepts.gloss: The upstream fibre span that directly supplies optical input to the referenced unit.
concepts.example: A break in the feeding fibre leaves the line amplifier input dark.

concepts.label: the preceding amplifier
concepts.gloss: The immediately upstream optical amplifier whose output feeds the current unit or span.
concepts.example: The preceding amplifier fails, so no light reaches the next receiver.

concepts.label: at the input of the multiplex section
concepts.gloss: The input boundary of a multiplex section where the combined WDM signal is launched or connected.
concepts.example: An unplugged patch cord at the multiplex input prevents the section from receiving light.

concepts.label: the fibre section feeding the unit, not against the unit itself
concepts.gloss: The feeding fibre section to which an OSC-loss condition is attributed, explicitly excluding the reporting unit itself.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS on an inline amplifier is recorded against the upstream span, not against the amplifier hardware.

concepts.label: through the switch
concepts.gloss: The portion of an ODU route that traverses the internal cross-connect fabric of an OTN switch.
concepts.example: All ODUs passing through the failed switch are interrupted.

concepts.label: the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: The unintended endpoint or egress to which a misconfigured ODU is delivered.
concepts.example: A customer-A ODU appears at customer C's port, the wrong destination.

concepts.label: on the ODU path currently in use
concepts.gloss: The working or protection ODU route currently selected to carry the service.
concepts.example: A defect on the currently selected protection route affects the active service.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: Either of the two endpoint locations terminating a bidirectional service or ODU trail.
concepts.example: A client-port failure at either end can take down the service.

concepts.label: in an OTN switch along the ODU path
concepts.gloss: An OTN switch situated at some point along the end-to-end ODU trail.
concepts.example: A wrong cross-connect in an intermediate OTN switch sends the ODU to another client.

concepts.label: client port
concepts.gloss: The client-facing interface location at which customer traffic enters or leaves the OTN system.
concepts.example: CLIENT_SF is observed at the 100GE client port.

concepts.label: on the working ODU path
concepts.gloss: The primary ODU route normally selected to carry a protected service.
concepts.example: A fibre failure on the working path causes the selector to choose protection.

concepts.label: on the protection ODU path
concepts.gloss: The standby ODU route reserved to carry service after failure of the working route.
concepts.example: PROT_UNAVAIL is raised when the protection path loses signal.

concepts.label: this port
concepts.gloss: The particular local port that is reporting or experiencing the condition.
concepts.example: A hardware self-test identifies a serializer fault on this port.

concepts.label: this switch's fabric
concepts.gloss: The internal cross-connect fabric of the particular OTN switch under diagnosis.
concepts.example: A failed ASIC in this switch's fabric interrupts its ODUs.

concepts.label: OTN switch
concepts.gloss: The OTN switching node in which an ODU-routing or fabric condition is located.
concepts.example: Diagnostics localize the wrong cross-connection to the intermediate OTN switch.

concepts.label: available on nodes with the channel monitoring option
concepts.gloss: An availability constraint under which per-channel measurements are exposed only on nodes licensed or equipped with channel monitoring.
concepts.example: A ROADM with the channel-monitoring option reports power and OSNR for every wavelength.

concepts.label: All units
concepts.gloss: An availability class indicating that the measurement is supported across every applicable unit without an optional monitoring feature.
concepts.example: Every applicable VB unit reports errored seconds and OSC presence.

concepts.label: Units with the power monitoring option
concepts.gloss: An availability constraint limiting input, output, or received-power measurements to units equipped with the power-monitoring option.
concepts.example: A licensed amplifier reports total input and output power, while an unlicensed one does not.

concepts.label: Units with the advanced monitoring option
concepts.gloss: An availability constraint limiting advanced metrics such as OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, polarization rate, and pump current to suitably equipped units.
concepts.example: A unit with advanced monitoring reports DGD and polarization rate in addition to basic power.

concepts.label: Each client port reports client errored seconds in 15-minute bins.
concepts.gloss: The reporting capability by which each client port supplies client errored-second counts in 15-minute bins.
concepts.example: Port 3 reports 7 client errored seconds for 14:00–14:15.

concepts.label: Each client port reports client unavailable seconds in 15-minute bins.
concepts.gloss: The reporting capability by which each client port supplies client unavailable-second counts in 15-minute bins.
concepts.example: A down port reports 900 client unavailable seconds for a full 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: A degradation
concepts.gloss: A fault nature in which performance or margin worsens while some signal or service may remain available.
concepts.example: A 3 dB OSNR decline raises errors but does not immediately interrupt traffic.

concepts.label: Hard failure
concepts.gloss: An abrupt, complete failure that removes signal, output, equipment operation, or service rather than merely reducing performance.
concepts.example: A broken fibre instantly removes all received light.

concepts.label: A degradation, not an outage
concepts.gloss: A non-catastrophic impairment that reduces quality but does not constitute complete loss of signal or service.
concepts.example: A dirty connector raises pre-FEC BER while the client service remains up.

concepts.label: gradual or step degradation rather than an outage
concepts.gloss: A deterioration that develops progressively or as a discrete reduction in performance, rather than as a total outage.
concepts.example: Fibre loss increases by 4 dB after a bend and later worsens gradually.

concepts.label: slow, incipient condition
concepts.gloss: A slowly developing precursor condition that indicates likely future failure before immediate traffic impact.
concepts.example: Pump current climbs over several months while amplifier gain remains on target.

concepts.label: mostly just after provisioning changes
concepts.gloss: A fault occurrence pattern associated mainly with the period immediately following configuration or cross-connect changes.
concepts.example: ODU_TIM appears just after an operator provisions the ODU to the wrong egress port.

concepts.label: critical
concepts.gloss: The highest alarm priority used for conditions causing or threatening immediate major service or equipment loss and requiring urgent action.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS after a fibre cut is reported with critical severity.

concepts.label: minor
concepts.gloss: A lower-priority alarm severity for degradations, warnings, or redundancy changes that do not necessarily cause immediate service loss.
concepts.example: AMP_PUMP_EOL is minor because it warns of ageing while traffic may remain unaffected.

concepts.label: not alarmed
concepts.gloss: A status classification recorded for informational defect indications that do not themselves raise an active severity alarm.
concepts.example: A received ODU_AIS indication is reported but assigned not-alarmed severity.

concepts.label: major
concepts.gloss: A serious alarm priority below critical, used for substantial faults that require prompt attention but may not represent immediate total service loss.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS is major because supervisory communication is lost even if payload channels remain present.

concepts.label: Each channel leaving a degree is switched separately.
concepts.gloss: ROADM forwarding behavior in which each wavelength leaving a degree is selected and switched independently of other wavelengths.
concepts.example: A ROADM routes 193.1 THz west and 193.2 THz north from the same incoming degree.

concepts.label: When frame alignment is lost, the unit applies the G.798 consequent actions: an ODU alarm indication signal is inserted downstream on every ODU the OTU carries, and a backward defect indication is sent to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.gloss: The G.798 consequent behavior for OTU frame loss: insert ODU-AIS downstream on every carried ODU and send BDI toward the far-end transmitter.
concepts.example: When an OTU receiver loses framing, its three carried ODUs are replaced with AIS and the remote transmitter receives BDI.

concepts.label: The OTN switch carries an ODU alarm indication signal onwards on every ODU cross-connected through it.
concepts.gloss: OTN-switch behavior that transparently carries a received ODU alarm indication signal onward across every corresponding ODU cross-connection.
concepts.example: An OTN switch receiving AIS on two ODUs forwards AIS through both configured egress cross-connects.
